questions: The core.h header must have extern "C" linkage for the C functions. The diff shows the declarations but not the extern "C" wrapper - is it present in the unchanged portion of the file?

The old code used std::atomic<bool> g_initialized with compare_exchange_strong for thread-safe one-time initialization. If any global state exists that requires initialization before first use, removing this thread-safety mechanism could cause data races. The comment claims 'core holds no global state that needs them' - can this be verified by examining all global/static variables in core/src/?
nits: The comment in core.h for ecuio_profile_registry_lookup still references ecuio_init in its lifetime description - should be updated to match the new comment style or verify it's still accurate.
The bridge's m_initialized member removal is clean, but consider if there's any diagnostic value in keeping track of initialization state for debugging purposes.
